---
id: c-dtw-gestures
title: Gesture Recognition with Banded Dynamic Time Warping
difficulty: Hard
order: 2
tags: dynamic programming, DTW, time series, robotics, 2-D tables
---
## Statement
A robot recognises hand gestures from a 1-D accelerometer trace. People perform gestures at different speeds, so a sample-by-sample comparison fails. **Dynamic Time Warping (DTW)** finds the cheapest monotone alignment between two sequences instead.

For sequences a (length n) and b (length m), with costs `|aᵢ − bⱼ|`:

```
D[0][0] = 0,  D[i][0] = D[0][j] = ∞   (i, j ≥ 1)
D[i][j] = |a[i] − b[j]| + min(D[i−1][j], D[i][j−1], D[i−1][j−1])     for 1 ≤ i ≤ n, 1 ≤ j ≤ m
DTW(a, b) = D[n][m]
```

A **Sakoe–Chiba band** of width w restricts the alignment: cell (i, j) may be used only if `|i − j| ≤ w`. Cells outside the band are ∞. If `w < |n − m|`, the end cell is unreachable and the distance is ∞.

Input:
- A line `T w`, then T templates, one per line: `name m v1 … vm`.
- A line `Q`, then Q queries, one per line: `m v1 … vm`.

Lengths are ≤ 2000, values are integers with |v| ≤ 10⁶, and T ≤ 10.

For each query, print one line:

`query K: name1=D1 name2=D2 ... -> BEST`

- Write `inf` for an unreachable distance.
- BEST is the template with the smallest distance, with ties going to the earliest template, or `none` if every distance is ∞.

Use an O(n·m) DP with rolling rows. The band only restricts which cells are valid.

## Starter
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void) {
    return 0;
}
```

## Hints
- Use `long long` and an `INF` like `LLONG_MAX / 4`, so `INF + cost` can't overflow.
- Two rows of length m + 1: `prev` for row i − 1 and `cur` for row i. Set every `cur[j]` to INF first, then fill only `j` in `[max(1, i − w), min(m, i + w)]`.
- `cur[0]` is INF for i ≥ 1. Only `D[0][0]` is 0.

## Solution
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <limits.h>

#define INF (LLONG_MAX / 4)

typedef struct { char name[32]; int m; long long *v; } Seq;

static long long dtw(const long long *a, int n, const long long *b, int m, int w) {
    if (abs(n - m) > w) return INF;
    long long *prev = malloc((size_t)(m + 1) * sizeof *prev), *cur = malloc((size_t)(m + 1) * sizeof *cur);
    for (int j = 0; j <= m; j++) prev[j] = INF;
    prev[0] = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j <= m; j++) cur[j] = INF;
        int lo = i - w > 1 ? i - w : 1, hi = i + w < m ? i + w : m;
        for (int j = lo; j <= hi; j++) {
            long long best = prev[j - 1];
            if (prev[j] < best) best = prev[j];
            if (cur[j - 1] < best) best = cur[j - 1];
            if (best >= INF) continue;
            long long d = a[i - 1] - b[j - 1];
            cur[j] = best + (d < 0 ? -d : d);
        }
        long long *t = prev; prev = cur; cur = t;
    }
    long long r = prev[m];
    free(prev); free(cur);
    return r;
}

static long long *read_seq(int m) {
    long long *v = malloc((size_t)m * sizeof *v);
    for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) if (scanf("%lld", &v[i]) != 1) exit(1);
    return v;
}

int main(void) {
    int T, w, Q;
    if (scanf("%d %d", &T, &w) != 2) return 1;
    Seq *tp = calloc((size_t)T, sizeof *tp);
    for (int k = 0; k < T; k++) {
        if (scanf("%31s %d", tp[k].name, &tp[k].m) != 2) return 1;
        tp[k].v = read_seq(tp[k].m);
    }
    if (scanf("%d", &Q) != 1) return 1;
    for (int q = 1; q <= Q; q++) {
        int m;
        if (scanf("%d", &m) != 1) return 1;
        long long *v = read_seq(m);
        printf("query %d:", q);
        int best = -1; long long bestd = INF;
        for (int k = 0; k < T; k++) {
            long long d = dtw(v, m, tp[k].v, tp[k].m, w);
            if (d >= INF) printf(" %s=inf", tp[k].name);
            else printf(" %s=%lld", tp[k].name, d);
            if (d < bestd) { bestd = d; best = k; }
        }
        printf(" -> %s\n", best < 0 ? "none" : tp[best].name);
        free(v);
    }
    for (int k = 0; k < T; k++) free(tp[k].v);
    free(tp);
    return 0;
}
```

DTW is the edit-distance recurrence moved to real-valued signals. Each step either advances both sequences (a match) or holds one of them while the other advances (a stretch), paying the local difference each time. The band does two jobs:
- It caps how far the alignment may warp, which stops pathological matches where one sample is aligned to half the other sequence.
- It cuts the cost from O(nm) to O(n·w).

Applications include gesture and speech recognition, comparing robot trajectories executed at different speeds, and aligning sensor logs. Rolling rows keep memory at O(m). To recover the alignment path itself, you'd keep the full table, or store one direction byte per cell and backtrack.
